summary_zh.motivation: 研究重扫描次数对选区激光熔化Ti6Al4V性能的影响

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how rescanning cycles affect the characteristics of Ti6Al4V produced by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Experiments were conducted with varying rescanning cycles, and samples were characterized by density, hardness, surface roughness, and microstructure.
summary_en.result: Rescanning cycles significantly influence densification and surface quality, with an optimal number improving material properties.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed through experimental measurements and microstructural analysis.

papers.title: Osseointegration effects of local release of strontium ranelate from implant surfaces in rats.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Numerous studies have reported the beneficial effects of strontium on bone growth, particularly by stimulating osteoblast proliferation and differentiation. Thus, strontium release around implants has been suggested as one possible strategy to enhance implant osseointegration. AIM: This study aimed to evaluate whether the local release of strontium ranelate (Sr-ranelate) from implants coated with mesoporous titania could improve bone formation around implants in an animal model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Mesoporous titania (MT) thin coatings were formed utilizing the evaporation induced self-assembly (EISA) method using Pluronic (P123) with or without the addition of poly propylene glycol (PPG) to create materials with two different pore sizes. The MT was deposited on disks and mini-screws, both made of cp Ti grade IV. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was performed to characterize the MT using a Leo Ultra55 FEG instrument (Zeiss, Oberkochen, Germany). The MT was loaded with Sr-ranelate using soaking and the drug uptake and release kinetics to and from the surfaces were evaluated using quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (QCM-D) utilizing a Q-sense E4 instrument. For the in vivo experiment, 24 adult rats were analyzed at two time points of implant healing (2 and 6 weeks). Titanium implants shaped as mini screws were coated with MT films and divided into two groups; supplied with Sr-ranelate (test group) and without Sr-ranelate (control group). Four implants (both test and control) were inserted in the tibia of each rat. The in vivo study was evaluated using histomorphometric analyses of the implant/bone interphase using optical microscopy. RESULTS: SEM images showed the successful formation of evenly distributed MT films covering the entire surface with pore sizes of 6 and 7.2 nm, respectively. The QCM-D analysis revealed an absorption of 3300 ng/cm2 of Sr-ranelate on the 7.2 nm MT, which was about 3 times more than the observed amount on the 6 nm MT (1200 ng/cm2). Both groups showed sustained release of Sr-ranelate from MT coated disks. The histomorphometric analysis revealed no significant differences in bone implant contact (BIC) and bone area (BA) between the implants with Sr-ranelate and implants in the control groups after 2 and 6 weeks of healing (BIC with a p-value of 0.43 after 2 weeks and 0.172 after 6 weeks; BA with a p-value of 0.503 after 2 weeks, and 0.088 after 6 weeks). The mean BIC and BA values within the same group showed significant increase among all groups between 2 and 6 weeks. CONCLUSION: This study could not confirm any positive effects of Sr-ranelate on implant osseointegration.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及植入物表面涂层释放锶来促进骨整合，但未涉及增材制造、多孔结构或力学测试。
llm.why_not_core: No LPBF fabrication, no porous structure design, no mechanical testing, no stress shielding analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究局部释放雷奈酸锶是否促进钛植入物骨整合。
summary_zh.method: 在钛表面涂覆介孔二氧化钛膜负载锶，植入大鼠胫骨。
summary_zh.result: 2周和6周后，锶释放组与对照组的骨整合无显著差异。
summary_zh.validation: 大鼠体内植入后组织形态学分析。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate whether local release of strontium ranelate from mesoporous titania-coated implants enhances peri-implant bone formation in rats.
summary_en.method: Mesoporous titania films with two pore sizes were coated on titanium disks and miniscrews, loaded with Sr-ranelate, and implanted in rat tibiae.
summary_en.result: Histomorphometric analysis showed no significant differences in bone-implant contact and bone area between Sr-loaded and control groups at 2 and 6 weeks.
summary_en.validation: In vivo rat model with histomorphometric analysis of the bone-implant interface.
